ambiguities_and_risks.description: The 3D-noise round-trip tolerance (5%) is statistically tight for the small components (t = 0.02, tv/th = 0.05 of sigma_TVH) at 100-200 frames; a purely relative tolerance may fail on estimator noise rather than physics.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Monte-Carlo the estimator on synthetic cubes to measure its standard error per component at 64x64x200; set relative 5% for components >= 0.08 and an absolute 0.02 sigma_TVH floor for smaller ones, recorded in the ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Warp kernel tests: Warp runs on CPU without CUDA, but warp is not in pyproject dependencies and must never be imported from tests/unit (VAL-06 will enforce this). Where those tests live and what marker gates them is undecided.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Prototype one kernel test under Warp's 'cpu' device in a scratch venv; if it works without CUDA, define a `warp` marker and CI job; otherwise keep `gpu`.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The unit suite must stay under 30 s (CLAUDE.md). Tier 2 benches (100-200 frames x 64x64 through six stages, Simpson over 16001 temperatures, slant-edge at 1024x1024 supersample) can blow the budget; the `slow` marker exists but is never deselected by `make test`.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Run `pytest tests/unit --durations=15` after each Tier 2 item; mark > 1 s tests `slow` and decide whether `make test` deselects `slow` (it currently does not) — record in VAL-01 or VAL-05.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §15 line 1181 says 'dL/dT vs finite difference < 1e-5 relative' without saying spectral or in-band; the existing test covers the spectral derivative at 1e-6, the ir-radiometry skill (line 111) wants the in-band dLb_dT vs FD of Lb. Only the in-band version validates the LUT's derivative table that NETD divides by.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Keep the spectral test and add the in-band test in VAL-07; both at <= 1e-5.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The G-buffer key set in tests/conftest.py (temperature_k, normal_dot_view, distance_m, material_id, sky_view_factor) is narrower than the §13.3 AOV table (full Normal vector, MotionVectors, SemanticSegmentation). If the Isaac adapter emits a different schema, kernel-vs-reference tests will compare different inputs.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Freeze the schema in VAL-03 with a test, and make the irsim_isaac annotator adapter's output pass the same schema test (import the checker from tests or from irsim.validation).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §6.1's displayed equation has (1 - alpha_sol)^c Q_sol while the prose (line 363) and §6.4 use alpha_sol Q_sol. The Tier 1 equilibrium test's analytic root depends on which is used.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Use alpha_sol Q_sol (spec prose, thermal-solver skill line 26) in VAL-09 and cite the line; ask the spec owner to fix the displayed equation.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Tier 3 'departed vehicle leaves a warm tyre trace and cool body shadow' and 'FFC freezes the image' require scene-level scripting (overlay model, scheduler) that no area has clearly claimed; without an owner the checklist item cannot be automated.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Assign the heat-trace overlay to the thermal area and the FFC scheduler to isp/noise in the roadmap; VAL-17 and VAL-20 depend on them explicitly.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Tier 5 (train a detector) is outside what this repo can test; the README Tier column has a T5 that nothing here can ever mark green.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide via ADR that T5 is an external protocol documented under docs/validation/, and reserve the README column for reports, not tests.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: ir-radiometry skill (line 65-66) says LUTs are checked into data/lut with a hash, but .gitignore ignores data/lut/*.npy and *.json. Either every developer must run `make luts` (and the hash-staleness path becomes the norm) or the ignore rules are wrong. Affects the staleness tests in VAL-07.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide (radiometry ADR) and make VAL-07's stale-LUT test exercise the real workflow: delete data/lut, run `make luts`, run the suite.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core — enforced today by tests/unit/test_layering.py (AST scan for omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb over src/irsim); VAL-06 extends it to forbid irsim -> irsim_isaac and to keep tests/unit free of engine imports so `make test` never needs a GPU.

#2 float32 or better wherever temperature/radiance flows — no test exists today (CLAUDE.md claims one). VAL-04 adds the fp32 encode/decode round trip (< 10 mK) with an fp16 sensitivity proof and a public-API dtype walk; VAL-03 asserts fixture dtypes; VAL-05 refuses float16 golden files; VAL-07 asserts LUT .npy dtype float32; VAL-23 asserts the AOV dtype and round trip in Isaac.

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin — enforced by VAL-13: NETD(373 K)/NETD(300 K) must equal dLb_dT(300)/dLb_dT(373) within 5% (a flat NETD fails), and radiance-domain sigma must be scene-temperature independent to 2%.

#4 Kirchhoff closure for every material in every band to 1e-6 — no test exists today (CLAUDE.md claims one). VAL-08 walks configs/materials x configs/sensors bands and also asserts the loader refuses double-authored properties.

#5 Aperture factor pi/(4F^2+1) defined once in irsim.optics — VAL-10: aperture_factor(1.0) == pi/5 to 1e-12, focal-plane irradiance known answer 0.628319 W/m^2, detector and self-emission proven to route through the same function, AST scan for hand-written 4F^2 outside irsim.optics.

#6 One WeatherSeries feeds thermal and atmosphere — VAL-11: constructors require the shared object (identity-checked), no file I/O inside the thermal/atmosphere models, and T_air/RH used by path radiance and convection agree to 1e-9 at every timestamp.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: Stefan-Boltzmann tolerance is stated three ways: docs/physics-model.md §15 line 1178 says 1e-6; .claude/skills/ir-sim-testing/SKILL.md line 52 says 1e-12 relative for 'Analytic identities (Planck forms, Stefan-Boltzmann)'; tests/unit/test_planck.py line 42 asserts 2e-5 with a comment but no ADR, although SKILL.md lines 61-62 require an ADR for a loosened physics tolerance.

§15 line 1184 places 'Temperature encode/decode round trip < 10 mK' in Tier 1 ('no scene, no renderer'), but §13.3 line 984, §16.4 line 1299 and isaac-sim-spg SKILL.md lines 111-113 define it as an Isaac AOV test in tests/integration/test_temperature_encoding.py.

CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2 says 'There is a test for the encode/decode round trip; keep it passing' and #4 says 'There is a test that walks the whole material library; keep it passing' — neither test exists (tests/ contains only conftest.py, test_layering.py, test_planck.py).

Makefile line 30 runs `pytest tests/golden -q --update-golden` but no conftest registers `--update-golden`; verified to error with 'unrecognized arguments'. ir-sim-testing SKILL.md line 108 tells people to use it.

CLAUDE.md layout says tests/golden holds regression fixtures and the step rule says `make check` must be green, but Makefile `test` runs only tests/unit, so tests/golden is never executed by `make check`; it runs only under `make test-all`, which CLAUDE.md says needs Isaac Sim.

pyproject.toml declares numpy>=1.24 but tests/unit/test_planck.py lines 37, 64-65, 80 use np.trapezoid (NumPy >= 2.0 only); on NumPy 1.26 three tests error. CHANGELOG.md 'Analytic identity tests passing' is untrue on the declared floor.

ir-sim-testing SKILL.md line 96 requires at least five G-buffer fixtures (uniform, ramp, two-material split, grazing-angle sphere, step edge); tests/conftest.py provides only gbuffer_ramp and gbuffer_uniform.
tests/unit/test_layering.py FORBIDDEN includes `carb`; CLAUDE.md #1 and src/irsim/__init__.py list only omni, pxr, isaacsim, warp. Neither forbids `irsim` importing `irsim_isaac`.

§15 line 1181 'dL/dT vs finite difference < 1e-5 relative' does not say spectral or in-band; test_planck.py line 57 tests the spectral form at 1e-6; ir-radiometry SKILL.md line 111 specifies the in-band dLb_dT vs FD of Lb, which is the one NETD depends on and is untested.

§15 line 1192 says decompose '100+ frames'; sensor-noise-chain SKILL.md line 164 says 200 frames and adds a 5% tolerance the spec does not state. §15 line 1182 gives no Kirchhoff tolerance; CLAUDE.md #4 and ir-sim-testing line 57 give 1e-6.
§6.1 line 355 displays absorbed solar as (1 - alpha_sol)^c Q_sol while line 363 and §6.4 line 406 (and thermal-solver SKILL.md line 26) use alpha_sol Q_sol; the equilibrium test must pick one.
ir-radiometry SKILL.md lines 65-66 say generated LUTs are 'checked into data/lut/' with a config hash, but .gitignore ignores data/lut/*.npy and data/lut/*.json.

§15 Tier 2 SITF/NETD/MTF require comparison with 'the real camera's measured curve' and 'datasheet within 10%', but every Boson noise/optics value in configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml is marked ESTIMATED and data/ holds no measurements, so the spec's Tier 2 pass criteria cannot currently be evaluated against reality.

README.md status table shows a Tier column including T5, and the ir-sim-testing skill says smoke tests must not count toward it; nothing in the repo defines what evidence promotes a component to T2-T5, and Tier 5 cannot be tested inside this repo at all.

§15 line 1191 NETD bench formula NETD = dT*sigma_noise/dDN implicitly assumes a linear DN(T) over dT; §9.4 line 669 defines it via the derivative. Consistent only if dT is small (few K) — the bench must state dT and check linearity (VAL-12 does).
